name: Borehole
author: Erin Carter
description: A geological borehole seen straight down from above, plunging to a true-black focal point at screen center. Fine sedimentary bands of faintly glowing rock are sliced from log-radius, scuffed by angular drill-grain, and tinted through the palette by depth; an exponential fog drowns the deep walls in black. The whole stack of strata sinks steadily down the scale axis toward a center it never reaches — nothing rotates, nothing translates.

params.label: Descent speed
params.effect: Scale-octaves per second the strata sink toward the dark center of the bore.

params.label: Band density
params.effect: Sediment bands per scale octave — higher packs finer, more numerous rings down the wall.

params.label: Fog depth
params.effect: How far down the bore light reaches before black swallows the walls; low values shrink the lit annulus toward the rim.

params.label: Grain
params.effect: Amount of angular drill-grain scuffing the bands — 0 leaves clean concentric rings.
